reason: The contract (problem.txt) explicitly requires each output to equal the real sigmoid value rounded ONCE to FP16 with round-to-nearest-even, exact bit patterns, for the whole public domain, and states one failing legal input is evidence against the implementation. Claim c1 is confirmed by an exhaustive sweep of all 63,488 finite FP16 inputs (t9): 7 legal inputs near zero (x = ±0.001..±0.011, where 1+exp(-|x|) ≈ 1 loses precision in FP32) produce wrong FP16 bit patterns, mpmath-verified against the true single-rounded value (e.g., x=0.0029296875: kernel 14338 vs required 14337). This is an in-scope, input-domain-covering defect against the contract's explicit exact-rounding clause — the deviation is a genuine rounding violation, not a declared-tolerance artifact. Claims c2 (negative-tail subnormal/underflow behavior: 0 mismatches across all 12,288 x<=-16 inputs, subnormals preserved, positive zeros only) and c3 (edge inputs and non-multiple-of-256 N: all bit-exact) are rebutted. All open claims have evidence and the Skeptic recorded no new claims after reviewing the latest evidence.
